# requireValidEmail

<link-summary>Returns the value as an email address, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireValidEmail() — Returns the value as an email address, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/string</code> · Since: 1.0.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireValidEmail(email: string | null | undefined, message?: string): string;
```

The address is split at a single `@`: the domain is checked the way `isValidDomain` checks one, and the local part must be non-empty and free of spaces. It is a format check, not proof that the mailbox exists.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter              | Type                          | Description                                                                       |
| :--------------------- | :---------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `email`                | `string \| null \| undefined` | The string value representing an email to validate. Can be `null` or `undefined`. |
| `message` _(optional)_ | `string`                      | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted.                     |

## Returns

`string` — the same value, typed as an email address.

## Throws

| Exception                     | Condition                          |
| :---------------------------- | :--------------------------------- |
| `InvalidEmailFormatException` | the value is not an email address. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireValidEmail("user@example.com"); // => "user@example.com"
requireValidEmail("first.last@sub.example.co.uk"); // => "first.last@sub.example.co.uk"
requireValidEmail("user@@example.com"); // throws InvalidEmailFormatException
requireValidEmail("user@"); // throws InvalidEmailFormatException
```
